title: Entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes: bounds and constructions with availability
abstract: In this work, we define entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes with availability, in which any set of up to $δ-1$ erased qudits can be recovered from any one of $t$ local recovery sets, each of size at most $r+δ-1$, with the recovery sets intersecting exactly in the erased coordinates, where $r$ is a (small) positive integer. We show that shared entanglement permits $t>1$, meaning that multiple local recovery sets can be available for the same set of up to $δ-1$ erasures. We establish a Singleton-like bound for this family of codes and present random constructions based on classical linear codes with Vandermonde parity-check matrices. We also provide explicit constructions of entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes with availability from several classical code families and their folded versions, including Tamo-Barg codes, fiber-product codes, and algebraic-geometry codes such as one-point Hermitian and Suzuki codes.
summary: This paper develops the theory and constructions for entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes (EAQLRCs) with availability. It establishes fundamental bounds and provides explicit examples derived from algebraic geometry codes, showing how shared entanglement allows for multiple independent recovery sets. This advances the field of fault-tolerant quantum memory by offering robust coding schemes for erasure correction.
main_problem: The work focuses on defining, bounding, and constructing entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes (EAQLRCs) that allow for fault tolerance against erasures.
main_result: They establish a Singleton-like bound for EAQLRCs and provide explicit constructions using various classical code families, including those derived from algebraic geometry curves.
method: The authors use techniques from classical coding theory (e.g., linear codes, folding) combined with quantum information concepts to construct the codes and derive their parameters.
model_or_system: The model is abstract quantum error correction applied to data storage, specifically addressing erasure channels where the location of lost qubits is known. The underlying mathematical structures are based on classical linear codes and algebraic geometry curves over finite fields.
key_observables: Code parameters such as length ($n$), quantum dimension ($k_Q$), locality ($r$), availability ($t$), and minimum distance ($d_{EA}$).
important_parameters: The key parameters are the erasure tolerance ($\delta-1$) and the number of local recovery sets available ($t$). The construction relies on shared entanglement.
main_assumptions: The definition assumes an erasure model where the positions of lost qubits are known. A major assumption is that the receiver's halves of the ebits are not subject to noise.
figures_summary: The notes mention comparative tables (Table 1 and Table 2) summarizing dimension bounds and parameters for different types of quantum local recovery codes derived from various classical families.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by reviewing necessary background in coding theory, formally defining EAQLRCs with availability, presenting random constructions using Vandermonde matrices, detailing explicit constructions from algebraic-geometry codes (like Hermitian and Suzuki), and concluding with open problems.
why_interesting: This work directly contributes to the theoretical framework of quantum data storage and fault tolerance, providing concrete construction methods that improve upon standard Quantum CSS code limitations by incorporating shared entanglement for enhanced local repair capabilities.
